page: Amazon Web Services t3.medium is a burstable general purpose virtual machine hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, giving a ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 35 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. It includes no dedicated GPUs, no bundled local storage, and registers a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements position the t3.medium within the lower tiers across compute, memory, and application-level workloads. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance generated a Geekbench single-core score of 858.0 and a multi-core score of 1125.0, with a PassMark CPU score of 1651.12 and stress-ng multi-core output of 1381.86. Memory bandwidth measured 10.18 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 8.4 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the server achieved 1.65 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 1.69 GB/sec in static web serving, and managed small 135M parameter LLM inference at 28.48 tokens per second during text generation.

The primary tradeoff of the t3.medium centers on its burstable CPU allocation model and entry-level resource capacity. Because baseline compute and network allocations are modest, the server relies on accumulated CPU credits to handle usage spikes. While this structure offers cost efficiency for low-utilization scenarios by avoiding the resource overhead of dedicated-core instances, continuous CPU or I/O stress depletes credits and degrades sustained throughput. Consequently, the instance is engineered for lightweight development environments, microservices, small staging servers, code compilation tasks, and low-traffic web applications rather than high-concurrency production workloads.
